# Hermit logo

The mark is a hermit crab carrying a shell drawn as a terminal window, with `++`
in place of pupils. The double meaning is structural rather than decorative: a
hermit crab carries a shell it did not grow, and Hermit wraps a local model in a
confined shell that *reduces* its authority instead of inheriting it.

**The SVGs are the source of truth.** Every PNG and the `.ico` are generated by
`build.sh`; none of them is edited by hand.

## Files

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `hermit.svg` | full mark on the charcoal ground |
| `hermit-alpha.svg` | full mark, transparent, with a drawn contour |
| `hermit-small.svg` | simplified mark for 32px and below |
| `hermit-small-alpha.svg` | simplified mark, transparent |
| `hermit-badge.svg` | full mark in a rounded square |
| `build.sh` | rasterizes all of the above |

Generated: `hermit-master.png` (2048²), `hermit-transparent.png` (2048², alpha),
`hermit-icon-{512,256,128,64,48,32,16}.png`,
`hermit-icon-{512,256,128}-alpha.png`, `hermit-badge-512.png`,
`hermit-readme-{320,200}.png`, `favicon.ico` (16/32/48).

```sh
./build.sh          # needs rsvg-convert and ImageMagick 7
```

## Two tiers

The full mark holds down to 48px. At 32 and below the crab's legs and eyestalks
are sub-pixel and turn to mush, so `hermit-small.svg` drops to the two elements
that survive — the shell whorl and the cursor. `build.sh` switches tiers
automatically; 32 and 16 come from the simplified mark.

## Palette

These are **definitional**, not sampled. They are the values in the SVG source,
so there is exactly one correct value per role.

| role | hex | where |
|---|---|---|
| ground | `#2C2D32` | page and badge ground |
| frame | `#31818A` | shell wall, window bezel |
| interior | `#12262C` | terminal screen |
| body | `#F2E7D5` | crab |
| accent | `#9FD49C` | cursor, underscore, `++` eyes |
| contour | `#2C2D32` | outline on the transparent variants |

## Contrast

| pair | ratio | |
|---|---|---|
| frame / ground | **3.03:1** | clears 3:1; this is what delineates the shell |
| frame / interior | **3.46:1** | the bezel reads against the screen |
| accent / interior | **9.24:1** | phosphor on a dark terminal |
| body / ground | **11.23:1** | |
| accent / ground | **8.09:1** | |
| body / frame | 3.70:1 | |
| contour / body | **11.23:1** | what makes the transparent variant work on light |

Transparent variants, contour against the page:

| page | contour | frame |
|---|---|---|
| white | 13.74:1 | 4.53:1 |
| GitHub light `#F6F8FA` | 12.91:1 | 4.25:1 |
| GitHub dark `#0D1117` | 1.38:1 | 4.18:1 |
| Gitea dark `#1E1F22` | 1.20:1 | 3.64:1 |

The contour is deliberately the same value as the ground. On a dark page it
disappears and the mark looks exactly as it does on its own ground; on a light
page it defines the crab, which is otherwise `#F2E7D5` on white at 1.22:1.

### One number went down, on purpose

Interior against ground is **1.14:1**, where the previous artwork was 1.38:1.
That is not a regression that slipped through — it is the fix.

Both the ground and a terminal screen are dark, so the interior cannot win a
contrast fight against the ground without becoming a lit panel: pushing it to
3:1 costs the phosphor green, which falls to 2.73:1 and stops reading as a
cursor. Lifting it partway is worse than either end — at `#2A6675` the bezel
collapses into the screen at 1.42:1 and the terminal loses its structure.

So the shell is delineated by the **frame** at 3.03:1, and the screen is pushed
darker so the cursor reads at 9.24:1. A dark screen fully enclosed by a bezel
that clears 3:1 is a terminal. A mid-tone panel is not.

## What changed from the first version

The artwork was generated, then traced to vector by colour layer. The geometry
is authored now, so:

- the palette is definitional rather than sampled — the old table named
  `#297072` for the shell frame where `#2B7173` covered 39x more pixels
- interior/frame contrast is chosen rather than inherited
- the transparent variants have a real contour
- 32 and 16 are a purpose-drawn mark instead of a downscale
- the raster set is 628 KB, down from 2,524 KB, and any size can be regenerated

The generated source carried C2PA provenance and a SynthID marker. Tracing
discards the pixels entirely, so nothing of that survives into these files —
verified with `aiscrub scan`, which `build.sh` also runs over its own output
because rsvg and ImageMagick both stamp metadata of their own.

## Regenerating

Edit the SVG, run `./build.sh`, commit both. Do not hand-edit the PNGs.
